_README: Frozen pulse-streamer deployment manifest -- the SINGLE source describing the geometry
already programmed on the qualified board.  The Python host reads it for validation and
the server also verifies the matching LAYOUT_FINGERPRINT from hardware.  It is not a
runtime tuning surface.  Only a separately approved, evidence-driven RTL recovery may
change these values, regenerate zlc_geometry.vh/geom.tcl, rebuild, and requalify hardware.
estimate_resources.bat may inspect a proposed recovery geometry; it grants no authority
Every 'params' field is folded into the geometry FINGERPRINT (CTRL word 63) except the
host-only cap ttl_delay_max_ticks, so a host packing for one geometry REFUSES a bitstream
built for another.  Editing this file alone only makes startup fail; it never changes the
running FPGA.  The explicit board.lanes indices generate the host target and validate
both the RTL top mapping and XDC; declaration order in either projection has no meaning.
See '_field_docs' below for what each field means.  '_README' and '_field_docs' are
documentation only -- geometry loading consumes params/fpga_part/clock_hz/target_pct,

_field_docs.fpga_part: Xilinx part string (e.g. xc7a35tfgg484-2).  Selects the resource budgets (LUT/FF/DSP/RAMB36) the estimator checks against and the synthesis target.
_field_docs.clock_hz: FPGA fabric clock in Hz.  50 MHz -> 20 ns per tick.  THE single source for the compile + runtime tick rate (all timing is in ticks); must equal the board oscillator + the XDC create_clock.
_field_docs.target_pct: Resource-budget target for estimate_resources (percent of each resource the geometry may use).  The capacity report flags any axis over this.
_field_docs.channel_count: Number of digital TTL output channels the bitstream drives (real outputs + DAC bus-member bits + da_clk pins).  Normally inferred from board.xdc; sizes the edge mask, the per-signal delay region, and num_delay_ch.  Pin-coupled: changing it needs an XDC + port-list edit, not just this value.
_field_docs.num_slots: Number of affine SCAN slots (s0..s{n-1}).  Every edge/bus tick = base + (sum_j coeff_j * slot_j) >> coeff_frac_bits, so one scan point sets all slots.  HARD CONSTRAINT: num_slots * coeff_width must equal 64 (the coeff BRAM packs 2 x 32-bit words).
_field_docs.coeff_width: Signed bit width of each affine coefficient.  16 -> coeff_bits = num_slots*16 = 64.  See the num_slots*coeff_width == 64 constraint.
_field_docs.tick_width: Bit width of an edge tick (the 20 ns-resolution timestamp).  Fixed at 32 (the tick BRAM + CTRL words are 32-bit); 32 bits ~= 85 s of program length at 50 MHz.
_field_docs.coeff_frac_bits: Fixed-point FRACTION the affine scan math shifts by (>> coeff_frac_bits).  The scan COMPILER scales coefficients by exactly this, so it MUST match the synthesized RTL or the emitted ticks disagree with the bitstream.
_field_docs.max_edges: Maximum number of edges (state-change rows) in one program.  Power of two; sizes the three parallel edge BRAMs (tick 32b / coeff 64b / mask 62b).  4096 -> EDGE_ADDR_WIDTH = 12.  Bigger = more BRAM (watch the RAMB36 budget).
_field_docs.bank_size: Scan points per ping-pong bank. TWO banks form the resident streaming window: the host freezes the complete logical table before FIRE, preloads the first two chunks, then refills each released bank while the FPGA remains the point-timing owner. This is a physical bank/chunk and refill-slack bound, not a logical scan-length limit. Power of two; sizes the scan BRAM (2*bank_size deep).
_field_docs.bus_count: Number of analog DAC buses (each = bus_width parallel output bits + one da_clk latch strobe).  4 buses (dipole / bias_x / bias_y / bias_z on this board).
_field_docs.bus_width: Bits per DAC bus.  10 -> 1024 codes in OFFSET-BINARY: code 0 = negative full scale, 512 = 0 V (idle/safe), 1023 = +full scale.
_field_docs.bus_seg_addr_width: Address width of the per-bus segment TABLE: max_bus_segments = 1 << this = 64 segments/bus.  WARNING: this is an ABI / register-map parameter -- it sets the segment-table size and thus SHIFTS the R_DELAY region base.  Do NOT change it to save LUT (that desynchronizes host<->bitstream addressing); the check guards bus_count*(bus_seg_addr_width+1) <= 32 (the single BUS_COUNTS CTRL word).
_field_docs.bus_sel_width: Bits to select which scan slot a bus segment endpoint samples (value_select / stop_value_select), so a ramp can scan both endpoints.  Guarded: 2*bus_width + 2 + 2*bus_sel_width <= 32 (the bus flags word).
_field_docs.slot_mul_width: Bit width of the scan-slot operand into the affine DSP multiplier.  25 fits one DSP48E1 (25x18), bounding a raw scan value to +/-2^24 ticks (the coeff still scales it to the full 32-bit range).
_field_docs.evt_fifo_depth: Per-TTL-CHANNEL event-FIFO depth = max output TOGGLES in flight per channel while a delay is applied (out[t] = in[t-d]).  Power of two (ring pointer).  Deeper = denser delayable pulse trains, more distributed RAM (LUTRAM).  NOT the delay LENGTH (that is ttl_delay_max_ticks).
_field_docs.bus_evt_fifo_depth: Per-DAC-BUS segment-FIFO depth = max RESOLVED bus segments in flight while a bus delay is applied (density-independent: one dense ramp = 1 segment).  Power of two.  Set equal to evt_fifo_depth (64) so DAC and TTL delay capacity match.
_field_docs.delay_region_words: Reserved 32-bit words in the R_DELAY register region (one delay word per delay-eligible signal: channels then buses).  Must be >= channel_count + bus_count (= 66); 128 gives headroom and a stable layout across configs.
_field_docs.ttl_delay_max_ticks: HOST-side validation cap on a single output delay, in ticks (the 32-bit R_DELAY field; (1<<31)-1 ~= 42.9 s at 20 ns).  Host-only -- it is NOT folded into the fingerprint, so tuning it needs no rebuild.  The real working limit is toggles IN FLIGHT (the FIFO depths above), checked at compile time.
